Subject: POC trial: workload intake and next steps

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff.

Recap (what we heard)
- Goal: validate model quality and cost/latency for AcmeHealth in-product triage assistant (clinical triage routing).
- Success criteria (your priorities):

 95th pctl latency under 250ms for standard queries (target 200ms if possible)

 Quality: >= 90% accuracy on the evaluation set you'll provide (we'll share the eval runner)

 Cost target: keep inference cost under $0.03/token equivalent during POC (we'll report unit economics)

Evaluation plan
1) Fill out the attached workload intake template (poc_workload_template.xlsx) with real traffic samples and expected token lengths.
2) We'll provision a 2-week POC: 1 week dry-run with recorded metrics, 1 week live/in-public tests.
3) We'll run the Redwood eval harness on your labeled set and produce a scoreboard (accuracy, F1, hallucination rate).
4) Infra metrics: per-route RPS, concurrency, 50/95/99 latencies, token counts, cost per 1k tokens.

Ownership / timeline
- AcmeHealth: provide labeled eval set + filled workload template by EOD Thu (2027-04-29). Owner: Alex.
- Redwood (Marissa): schedule kickoff, finalize SLOs and test plan.
- Redwood (Ben): infra sizing and initial config for batching/quantization; deliver capacity estimate by Fri (2027-04-30).

Immediate ask
- Please attach the completed workload template and any sample request traces you can share (sanitized).

I'm attaching the intake template now. Ben, adding you for sizing comments.

Thanks,

Alex, quick notes to help you fill the template and what we need from the traces:

Workload profile fields to complete (example values included)
- Steady-state RPS: typical sustained requests per second (e.g., 5 RPS)
- Peak burst RPS: short bursts we need to absorb (e.g., 25-40 RPS for 1-3 minutes)
- Average token lengths: user prompt ~30-50 tokens, model response ~80-160 tokens
- Concurrency: active concurrent sessions (e.g., 30-100)
- Burst patterns: frequency (times/day), duration, ramp-up profile
- Request size distribution: percent of requests that are short (<=32 tokens), medium, long (>256 tokens)

How we use this
- Sizing: choose GPU type and batch sizing to meet latency SLOs while minimizing cost.
- Caching/batching strategy: if you have predictable prefixes we can leverage KV cache to lower costs.
- Quantization: we'll recommend quantized variants if quality vs. cost tradeoffs are acceptable.

Example intake (fill these into the sheet):
- steady_rps: 5
- peak_burst_rps: 40 (1-2 min, 2x/day)
- avg_prompt_tokens: 30
- avg_response_tokens: 120
- concurrency_expected: 50
- percent_long_requests: 8% (>256 tokens)

I'm attaching the template again and a small example CSV of anonymized traces we use for ramp testing.


Ben
Ben Carter

Marissa / Ben, thanks for the clear notes. I filled out the workload template and attached it (acmehealth_workload_answers.xlsx). Answers inline / key points below:

- Steady-state RPS: 6 RPS (expected during normal business hours)
- Peak bursts: up to ~40 RPS for 60-120s, typically 2x/day (morning sync and post-release validation)
- Avg prompt tokens: 28 tokens
- Avg response tokens: 160 tokens (we tend to include more context in responses)
- Concurrency: expected concurrency 30-60 active sessions
- Long requests (>256 tokens): ~6%
- Latency expectation: we prefer 200-250ms 95th but can tolerate 300ms for complex completions during POC

Attached: acmehealth_workload_answers.xlsx (filled template) and a short anonymized trace excerpt. Let me know if you need more context on ramp behavior.

Alex Tan
